alignments.note: The waw takes the connective Then written for it (rule 14).
Finite verb with an explicit subject noun standing separately.
עתה takes Now; no waw stands beside it here (rule 14).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun, inverted in the English (rules 17, 24).
Divine name, fronted as the English subject (rule 25).
Hiphil of יטב rendered as light verb plus complement, do ... good, headed on the complement and discontinuous around the object pronoun (rules 25, 44).
Dative לְ rendered as a bare English indirect object (rule 40).
The second כי takes the subordinator seeing written for it.
היה is present in the possessive clause and takes the have itself (rule 43).
Its preposition goes unrepresented under rule 43.

The ASV's recasting realizes this one suffix twice — as the subject pronoun of I have (rule 43) and again as the possessive my on priest — so both words are its one discontinuous unit, headed on the direct pronoun (rules 18, 25). The my is not added: rule 18's supplied-possessive sentence governs a phrase with no suffix in it, and the chapter's other two instances of this construction give the same possessive to the same suffix (17.5, 17.12: his priest).
The ASV renders the noun indefinitely and writes no the for the article (rule 29); the a is the noun's own (rule 15).
Indefinite a belongs to the noun (rule 15).
Resultative לְ takes the written to (rule 49).

review_notes: Reconciliation patch: only the suffix unit s014 and the removal of the added my change; every other unit is as the verse pass returned it.
Headed on I, the direct pronoun, rather than on the possessive recasting my, exactly as rule 18 heads מִכֶּם מָזוֹר -> cure you of your wound on you.
